voce: Across the Hudson River from Manhattan, in Jersey City, New Jersey, stood Knight Capital Group.
It was not a bank, and it was not a household name.
Yet in two thousand twelve, it was among the largest traders in American equities by volume.
That is according to the Securities and Exchange Commission, and to press reports at the time.
sotto: Per SEC filings and press reports

voce: Knight acted as a market maker, buying and selling stocks on behalf of brokerages.
Its customers also included retail investors, ordinary people placing everyday orders through their brokers.
oggetto: A row of glossy blue faceless mannequins standing in front of a large glowing stock chart

voce: Before the incident, the company's market value was reported at several hundred million dollars.
Its stock was trading near ten dollars a share.
didascalia: Approximate share price before the event

voce: A powerful, trusted engine of the markets, quietly running every trading day.
sotto: Millions of orders flowing through its systems

voce: But one morning, that engine would start doing something nobody had ever planned.
